name: Classical Sparta
title: Social Hierarchy of Ancient Sparta: From Kings to Helots
period: c. 600–371 BCE (to the defeat at Leuctra)

tiers.name: The two kings
tiers.you: You command Sparta’s army and offer the city’s sacrifices, but five ephors elected each year watch over you and can join in putting you on trial.
tiers.kid: Sparta had two kings at the same time, who led the army and offered sacrifices to the gods.
tiers.rise: The throne passed by birth within the two royal houses, but a king could be deposed: in 491 BCE Demaratus lost his throne after his fellow king Cleomenes I bribed the oracle at Delphi to declare him illegitimate, and he fled to Persia.
tiers.why: Sparta had two kings at once, one from each of two hereditary houses, the Agiads and the Eurypontids, both claiming descent from Heracles.

tiers.name: Spartiates
tiers.you: You have passed through the agoge, eat with about fifteen comrades in your common mess and live from land that helots farm for you; the law forbids you to trade or practise a craft.
tiers.kid: Spartiates were the citizens of Sparta, men who trained from boyhood to be soldiers.
tiers.rise: Birth, the agoge and election to a mess made a Spartiate. A man who could no longer pay his mess contributions, or who was judged a coward in battle, lost his full rights and fell among the inferiors.
tiers.why: The Spartiates, or homoioi (“equals”), were the full citizens.

tiers.name: Inferiors
tiers.you: You were born to Spartiate parents, but you can no longer pay your share to a common mess, so you have lost your vote and your place among the equals.
tiers.kid: Spartans who became too poor to pay for their shared meals lost their place as full citizens.
tiers.rise: Men fell into this rank through poverty, failure to win a place in a mess or cowardice in battle; with no regular way back, their number grew as land passed into fewer hands.
tiers.why: The inferiors (hypomeiones) were men of Spartiate descent who had lost, or never gained, full citizenship.

tiers.name: Foster brothers
tiers.you: You grew up in the agoge as the foster brother of Spartiate boys, your way paid by a wealthy family; you fight for Sparta and might rise to high command, but you are not one of the equals.
tiers.kid: Some boys who were not citizens were raised and trained with Spartan boys, and a few became famous commanders.
tiers.rise: A wealthy family’s sponsorship brought a boy into the agoge beside its own sons; some mothakes later became citizens, while others remained soldiers without a vote.
tiers.why: The mothakes, “foster brothers”, were boys of free birth but not of full Spartiate standing who were brought up in the agoge beside Spartiate boys, their costs usually paid by wealthy families.

tiers.name: Perioikoi
tiers.you: You live in your own town, farm your land or work as a craftsman or trader, and march with Sparta’s army when called, but you have no voice in how Sparta is ruled.
tiers.kid: The perioikoi were free people who lived in their own towns and made the weapons for Sparta’s army.
tiers.rise: Perioikoi were born to their status. Freed helots could be raised to a standing like theirs, but the agoge, and with it Spartan citizenship, was closed to their sons except by rare special permission.
tiers.why: The perioikoi, “those who dwell around”, were free Lacedaemonians who lived in their own towns, at least 33 of them in Laconia and Messenia.

tiers.name: Freed helots
tiers.you: You were born a helot and won your freedom by serving as a hoplite; you may be sent to fight far from home, and you will never be a citizen.
tiers.kid: Some helots were set free after serving as soldiers in Sparta’s army.
tiers.rise: Freedom came only by decision of the state, chiefly as the reward for service as a hoplite; it made a helot free, but never a citizen.
tiers.why: From the late 5th century Sparta freed helots in return for service as hoplites.

tiers.name: Helots
tiers.you: You and your family farm a Spartiate’s land and hand over part of the harvest, keeping the rest, and every year the ephors declare war on your people.
tiers.kid: Helots were people conquered by Sparta and forced to farm the land for Spartan citizens.
tiers.rise: Helots were born into their condition. Freedom came only from the state, chiefly as a reward for service as soldiers, until the Theban invasion that followed Leuctra freed the helots of Messenia in 370–369 BCE.
tiers.why: The helots were the subject people of Laconia and Messenia, descended from Greeks conquered by Sparta, above all the Messenians.
